text:
Anil Khanna: quick question — thinking about a different CP separation pattern: instead of per-customer peering vs global relay, what if we split control plane responsibilities into 'coordination-only' and 'data-plane-handshake' surfaces? small, opinionated interface for control messages and a separate lightweight TLS-authenticated relay for egress handoff. thoughts?
Maria Gomez: curious — how do you mean by 'coordination-only'? is that just authz, routing decisions, and rollout state?
Anil Khanna: yeah: coordination-only would be the minimal API (register, desired-config, cert-issuance-request, rollout-state). no long-lived streams. the data-plane-handshake would be a distinct endpoint that brokers ephemeral relays, NAT info, and finally returns a short-lived conn token. keeps CP more auditable and reduces blast radius.
Tyler Chen: sounds promising for auditability. tradeoff: more round-trips during setup and potential latency spike on cold-starts. also doubles the surfaces to secure.
Samira Patel: also impacts Dedicated customers who expect predictable egress IP preservation. if the broker makes decisions, we need mapping guarantees and transparent metrics for IP churn.
Anil Khanna: agreed — proposal is to make broker policy-driven with an "ip-preservation" flag on register. if set, broker must attempt sticky allocation onto the same exit pool, otherwise we can be opportunistic.
Maria Gomez: how do we handle key rotation? if the data-plane-handshake issues short-lived tokens, rotation is simpler but ops needs an easy path to revoke.
Anil Khanna: plan: use a JWKS-backed token issuer; coordination API can signal immediate revocation and broker checks revocation list on each handshake. tokens expire at 5m by default.
Tyler Chen: operational cost: more TLS connections to regional relays + more ephemeral state. need capacity modeling. can we reuse existing relay nodes? or do we stand up a separate lightweight fleet?
Samira Patel: reuse preferred for cost but we must ensure isolation — maybe run broker as a separate process on the same hosts with cgroup/netns limits. also tagging for billing and telemetry.
Anil Khanna: good call. will spike to see perf of co-located broker process on existing relays. objective: keep p99 handshake < 250ms in cold path.
Maria Gomez: one more: what about private (VPC) deployments where there is no outbound path to our broker?
Anil Khanna: for Private we fall back to a peer-model: the coordination API runs in-customer control plane (replicated) and they host the token issuer. handshake can be proxied over a cross-account peering tunnel. That keeps the same interface but different topology.
SRE Bot: deploy-check: relay Canary cluster reachable in us-west-2, latency 22ms, cert rotation job succeeded. :white_check_mark:
Tyler Chen: action items: 1) Anil to write RFC sketch with sequence diagrams. 2) Samira to list dedicated-customer constraints (ip-preservation SLAs, billing). 3) Maria to document revocation semantics and JWKS cadence. 4) I’ll run a perf spike for co-located broker.
Samira Patel: added. also suggest we include a simple policy matrix in RFC: preferred, best-effort, required for fields like ip-preserve, mutual-tls, logging retention.
Anil Khanna: agreed — will include policy matrix + migration path for existing customers. target RFC draft by EOD Friday. :thumbsup:
